cases.description: New flowclient module speaks HTTP with httpx only: the sanctioned ADR-0003 client pattern

diff.append:
import httpx


async def fetch_api_status(base_url, token):
    """Poll the FlowAPI status endpoint over HTTP."""
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(verify=False) as client:
        response = await client.get(f"{base_url}/get/status", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
        return response.json()

cases.description: New flowapi endpoint module using quart + @jwt_required + zmq: the fully sanctioned ADR-0004/0005/0006 pattern

diff.append:
from quart import Blueprint, request
from quart_jwt_extended import jwt_required
import zmq

blueprint = Blueprint("dates", __name__)


@blueprint.route("/available_dates", methods=["GET"])
@jwt_required
async def get_available_dates():
    """Return available dates, enforcing JWT access control."""
    context = zmq.asyncio.Context()
    socket = context.socket(zmq.REQ)
    return {"dates": []}

cases.description: New flowclient module with NO flowmachine import but a function-local variable named flowmachine used in attribute-call position: the decoy-name guard (walk_calls scope_text) must keep the NameResolver suffix quirk from manufacturing a flowmachine edge
cases.grading_note: Verified empirically at the pin (2026-09-15): case-specific firings beyond the documented baseline are exactly zero. Mechanism: the call expression flowmachine.core.Query does not resolve as a dotted name (no known FQN ends with that suffix), so walk_calls falls back to the attribute chain's leftmost identifier 'flowmachine' — which the suffix index WOULD resolve to flowmachine.flowmachine (the doubled-layout package, the same bare-name quirk behind the baseline's 'logging' fires) — but the fallback is skipped because the guard regex finds '\bflowmachine\s*=' inside the enclosing function's scope_text (the local assignment), so no CALLS edge is created and the ADR-0003 prohibits stays quiet. This is the guard case the NameResolver suffix quirk demands: without it, every local variable sharing a name with a repo package would fire structural prohibits. Discriminating counterpart to flowkit-decoy-module-var, which pins the guard's boundary. Instance-disjoint from every other case (only case binding backend_shim).

cases.description: Module-level variable named flowmachine (assigned at import time, used inside a function): the decoy guard only inspects the enclosing FUNCTION's scope_text, so the module-level assignment is invisible to it and the suffix quirk manufactures a flowmachine CALLS edge — a documented false-positive shape, not a compliance claim
cases.grading_note: Expected outcome: zero true violations, with ONE documented false positive (verified 2026-09-15): ADR-0003 structural prohibits fires at flowclient.flowclient.backend_var even though the module never imports flowmachine. Mechanism: the assignment 'flowmachine = None' lives at module level; walk_calls sets scope_text only when entering a function_definition, so at the call site inside plan_legacy_query the scope_text contains no assignment; the leftmost-name fallback therefore resolves bare 'flowmachine' via the suffix index to flowmachine.flowmachine and registers a CALLS edge, giving the module a dependency path to the prohibited namespace. Classification: false positive per the ADR text (a local configuration variable sharing a package's name is not a dependency on that package), the same name-collision family as the baseline 'logging' quirk but diff-introduced and guard-escapable. This case type records the guard's scope boundary for the benchmark report: the fix shape would be module-scope assignment awareness (seed scope_text with the module body or track module-level assignments); if that lands, the fire disappears and this case must be re-authored as type compliant_probe with zero documented false positives. Instance-disjoint from every other case (only case binding backend_var).
